description:
Estimate the cost of one or more home-improvement services for a US home.

    When to use: the homeowner wants to know what a job should cost, for
    example before asking contractors for bids.
    Limits: US residential homes only, one property per call. A planning
    estimate from national cost data with metro-area or state labor rates, not
    a bid; actual prices depend on the site, the scope and the local market.

    Args:
        home_sqft: Finished square footage of the home (200-20000).
        num_rooms: Number of rooms (1-50). Used to derive wall area.
        services: Services to price, e.g. ["painting", "roofing"].
        quality_tier: "economy", "medium" (mid-range) or "high" (premium).
        zip_code: 5-digit US ZIP code of the property. Applies metro-area (or
            state) labor-rate adjustments; strongly recommended.
        state: Two-letter state code, used when the ZIP is unknown.
        stories: Above-grade stories (1, 1.5, 2 or 3; default 1). Drives roof
            area, siding area and gutter length for exterior services.
        flooring_type: For flooring only: carpet, tile, vinyl, hardwood or mix.
        num_windows: For windows only: actual window count, if known.
        ceiling_height_ft: Override the default 8.5 ft ceiling height.
        roof_sqft: Override the roof area derived from home size.
        include_permits: Add estimated permit fees as separate lines.
        include_contingency: Add a 10% contingency line for conditions found on site.
        include_line_items: Include itemized quantities and unit costs.
        roof_pitch: Roof slope if known: low, standard, steep or very_steep.
            Steep roofs add area and a steep-slope labor surcharge.
        roof_shape: gable, hip or complex; sets the gutter/eave length.
        home_type: detached, townhouse_end, townhouse_middle or condo; shared
            walls reduce siding, trim and gutters (condo exteriors are flagged
            as usually the HOA's responsibility).
        year_built: Year the home was built. Before 1978 adds EPA lead-safe
            (RRP) work practices to painting, windows and drywall.
        Each property detail you pass narrows the likely range for the
        services it affects.

    Returns totals per service, a confidence range, the main assumptions, and
    questions to ask the homeowner that would tighten the estimate.
name: estimate_project
title: Estimate a home-improvement project
